Holding Court: SA's Rodeo Queen

By: Graham Coetzer | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We meet 22 year old Handrie van Bergen, a newcomer to the dangerous world of bull riding who has her eyes on the national Rodeo title and is showing the boys how to take the bull by the horns.

Unique Selling Point:
Meet the lady showing the men how to take the bull by the horns

Summary:
Handrie Beukes is a charming 22 year old bullrider who in her fisrt year of bullriding is currently ranked amongst the top 4 riders in the country - we go behind the scenes of the SA Rodeo scene.

Script:


Voice
The gate snaps open and this cowboy holds on for dear life. But this isn’t Texas, and this cowboy is in actual fact a cowgirl.

Link Mac
If you thought cowboys and cowgirls only exist in Texas or in western movies, well we’ve got our very own right here in South Africa.

Voice
Lassos, bucking bulls, country bling and lightning fast barrel races. Even the all important rodeo clowns. The South African bull riding scene is alive and kicking. We met rookie Handrie van Bergen at a rodeo training day held at the Que Sera arena on the outskirts of Pretoria. The petite 22 year might not look like your stereotypical bull rider - but don’t let her looks fool you - she’s as fearless as she is charming.

Sound Up Handrie
Mac: So Handrie when you get onto that bull, what’s going through your mind, is there a little prayer that you say is there music that’s playing in your head?

Handrie: Before I open I say please God help me, and then bam it comes up! And the song, that song of “Bad to the bone”

Mac: I’m bad to the Bone!

Voice
Or broken to the bone… Bull riding has been called “the most dangerous 8 seconds in sports”, and when we met van Bergen she was nursing a badly injured foot, courtesy of the last bull she rode.

Sound Up Handrie
It’s not like skydiving or bungee jumping, because you know what’s going to happen. With that bull when you sit on him, you don’t know what he’s going to do. Because you’re out of control.

Voice
The rules are simple. Riders are only allowed to hold on with one hand, with the aim being to last a full 8 seconds before falling off or dismounting. To make things safer for the bulls, riders have to dismount if they reach full time. The bulls are also judged on their performance in the arena, says Hachtor Beukes, president of SA Rodeo and one of the country’s most experienced bull riding judges.

Sound Up Hacthor
So if he’s got a lot of strength, agility, rhythm, change of direction, twisting in a buck, then he’s starting to get a good class rodeo bull.

Voice
Gauteng Roughstock club president Robert Willams says he’d like to see the sport grow into the massive spectacle seen in countries like the United States, where riders and bulls can earn thousands of dollars in prize money.

Sound Up Robert
A lot of people see it as ja ok, it’s just a nice thing that you go out for a day, but that’s not the case. This is an extreme sport like you see very seldom, and like those guys that you see with Red Bull extreme sports, that is what you see with our sport as well.

Voice
Events are held nationwide, and that’s where van Bergen, currently ranked amongst the top four riders in the country, is making her name. Growing up on a cattle farm in Hertzogville, she and older sister Sarina fell in love with horse riding. And it was Sarina who first tried her hand at bull riding.

Sound Up Handrie
It was great to see her ride, and it was an inspiration for me.

Voice
With Handrie being the accident prone baby of the family, her parents had their misgivings about her having a go.

Sound Up Handrie
And they told me you get this idea out of your head. And I was like ok.

Voice
But the bug had bitten, and at an event in Machadodorp her sister organised Handrie’s first bull ride - even though things didn’t go exactly as planned.

Sound Up Handrie
But I told her don’t tell mom and dad. So I got on the bull that day. And when he came out it was like a tamed horse just going in a circle. And the bell went off, and I came off, and I was like that wasn’t the first bull ride I had imagined.

Voice
But once she’d had her first ride on a ranked bull, she was hooked.

Sound Up Handrie
Handrie: They gave me a proper bull that jumped, and I felt it, and I liked it, and it’s where it all started.

Mac: And you’ve never looked back.

Voice
Training days like the one we attended are the ideal place for novice riders to learn the ropes from the old hands like top local rider Rikus Rossouw.

Sound Up Rikus
So when we are going to pull the rig, your pinkie is going to be in the middle of the rig.

Voice
We got to see Rossouw in action as he held on for the full 8 seconds on this notoriously grumpy, horned-monster of a bull affectionately known as Milo.

Sound Up Mac
Can you see the size of those horns, I’d never get on this bull. They call him Milo, there’s no milo here bru. This is coffee.

Sound Up Bull ride and Mac
That was unbelievable, I can’t believe this guy just did that. Wow!





Voice
19 year old Katlego Selolo is an up and coming cowboy with dreams of taking on the best in the world.

Sound Up Katlego
I want to see myself representing South Africa, that’s my goal.

Voice
An avid horse rider who learnt the craft from his father, Katlego says he’s ready to make the jump to bull riding. At the training camp we joined him for his second ever bull ride.

Sound Up Mac
This is probably one of the tensest periods, as you prepare for the longest eight seconds of your life. And this beast is about 800 kilograms strong.

Sound Up Katlego
Mac: So what do you your friends say, I mean you’re a black cowboy?

Katlego: It’s actually something new, like I’ve done it today, which was the best I’ve done, which was five seconds, the first time I did two seconds.

Voice
The sport has drawn criticism from animal rights activists both locally and internationally, but the participants say safety for both their animals and riders is ingrained in the cowboy way of life.

Sound Up Robert
For us it’s all about the animal’s safety, and then the rider’s safety. So we need to always make sure this is according to the book.

Voice
Monitoring the action at the event were members of both the SPCA and the Gauteng Department of Veterinary Services. Prior to being ridden, each bull is given a chance to stretch it’s legs and warm up. Beukes says training days are just as important for the animals as their riders.

Sound Up Hachtor
It’s very important for that animal to know exactly what you are going to do with him, because then he is more relaxed, and he’s going to start thinking, and he’s going to compete in the arena much better.

Voice
For the cowboys and girls, rodeo is synonymous with family time, and the youngsters also get to try tamer animals. Teenage brothers Eric and Kevin Jooste both braved bulls, as did Hachtor’s daughter, Chani Beukes.

Sound Up Chani Ride

Voice
As it’s still a growing sport in South Africa, there is no official women’s league in bull riding yet, which means that female competitors like Handrie have to compete against their male counter parts.

Sound Up Handrie
Handrie: Well I want to prove a point actually. I want to be an inspiration for women, younger generations. Just to say, hey….

Mac: We can also do this

Handrie: We can also do this.

Mac: If there’s cowboy’s, there’s definitely cowgirls?

Handrie: Ja!

Voice
Having qualified for the finals in December this year, Handrie has her sights set on becoming queen of the rodeo. And in case you’re wondering, she now has both mom and dad’s full blessing after achieving her first overall win at an event in Clarence.

Sound Up Handrie
I was the only women’s rider between six men I think. And then my mother and father was also there. So that night, we went and stood around the fire. And I told my dad, ok I’m finished bull riding because I did my goal, for the year. I won a rodeo. And he looked at me like this and he said no, no, no, you can ride two or three times more.

Voice
And her message to all the cowboys out there is clear….

Sound Up Mac
There’s definitely a new sheriff in town.






Promo 1
Voice
We meet the cowboys and -girls of the SA Rodeo scene, and one charming young woman who’s vying for the title of queen of the rodeo.

Promo 2
Voice
It’s a 150 year old tradition that’s been called the “most dangerous 8 seconds in sports”. Meet the cowgirl taking on the boys in the local Rodeo scene.

Promo 3
Voice
Lightning fast barrel races, country bling and death defying bull rides. South African cowboys and girls take us behind the scenes of the ultimate extreme sport.
